gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Avalon A4, ChatGPT's 'best value' pick, is missing from the current ENERGY STAR water-cooler list (Version 3.0, updated 2026-11-08), while Bob Vila calls it certified. They also don't state that the Brio 520 and Brio Moderna 720 share one ENERGY STAR test record: 0.76 kWh/day standby, 0.74 gal/h of cold water at 42°F and 46 six-ounce cups/h of hot water at 167°F. Avalon's own rating for the A4 is 2.5 L/h (0.66 gal/h) cold at ≤47°F and 4 L/h hot at ≥185°F, which is a different temperature basis.
standout_why: I compared against Bob Vila's page, the only page ChatGPT cited in both chats, opened 2026-11-10. It lists 'Energy Star: certified' for the Avalon A4, the Brio 500 Series and the Moderna. It gives no kWh/day, no cold gal/h, no hot cups/h and no temperature basis. Its only numbers are Moderna's adjustable range (39°F to 194°F) and an A4 test result of 'tea temperature in about 5 minutes'. So the cited rival has none of the normalised figures, and the ENERGY STAR finding contradicts its A4 claim. I stayed within the tool budget, so I did not open shouldit, mybest, Popular Mechanics or the other uncited results. Some of them may list maker ratings, but probably not ENERGY STAR test values.
decides: It confirms the Brio 520 ($329.99 on briowater.com today) as the pick whose numbers are verified. It also shows that the Moderna 720 ($449.99), which ChatGPT called 'best premium temperature control', tested the same as the 520. Both sit in one ENERGY STAR family with identical results, so the extra $120 buys the display, ozone cleaning and adjustable temperatures, not more cooling or heating. The Avalon A4 can stay the budget pick, but no one should call it ENERGY STAR certified. Its cold rating (0.66 gal/h at ≤47°F) is close to Brio's tested 0.74 gal/h at 42°F, but its standby kWh/day has no independent source. Primo's bottom-load family (601202 and others) shows exactly the same test values as the Brio 520 family: 0.76 kWh/day, 0.74 gal/h, 46 cups/h, 42°F and 167°F.

findings.note: Version 3.0 test. Type: Hot, Cook, and Cold; bottom-load bottle; High Capacity class. 0.76 × 365 = 277 kWh/yr with no water drawn. A separate query on additional_model_information LIKE '%CLBL720SC%' returned only pd_id 2399537 (Brio) and 2399677 (LAGO). That confirms the Moderna 720 is certified under this record.
